# Volume 5 — CHAPTER IX. IDA INTERVENES

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Miss Winifred held a conversation with Mr. Ashdown that resulted in quite a surprise for that preoccupied man. Without much deference, she drew his attention to how he had failed in his obligations by permitting a street child such as Mary Stubbs to enter his household and mingle with his offspring while remaining completely ignorant of her background.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0000 }

“Of course, I’m not claiming that a great deal of damage has been brought about,” she finished. “When everything is taken into account, this Mary-creature cannot really be considered wicked. Having interrogated the Carrows as well as your own offspring, I have gathered that no serious complaints can be raised regarding the girl, apart from her use of slang and unpolished expression. Nevertheless, consider the possible outcome had her character resembled certain home children within our acquaintance. You are personally aware of the things that unfortunate youngster at the Saul Flaggs’ instructed and imparted to the Flagg offspring.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0001 }

Mr. Ashdown was indeed aware, and he felt genuine shock regarding how careless he had been about the situation.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0002 }

“However, what can we do, Mrs. Kerr?” he inquired in a helpless manner. “Turning the poor child away is impossible. Caring for her is something that must be done.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0003 }

“Certainly. Writing to the Hopetown authorities immediately would be best. In the meantime, I guess she may just as well remain in this place for a couple of extra days until a response from them reaches us. However, stay alert, Mr. Ashdown.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0004 }

Tabitha’s death from horror would have occurred right there had Miss Winifred’s admonishment of a clergyman reached her ears. Miss Winifred, however, left filled with a heated sense of fulfillment regarding a performed duty, and when evening arrived, Mr. Ashdown requested that Mary join him inside his study. Looking truly dreadful from terror, Mary complied. Yet the impoverished, beaten little life she led received an unexpected turn. The gentleman who inspired such profound dread in her proved to be the most compassionate, softest spirit she had ever encountered. Mary discovered herself spilling every single one of her woes to him prior to realizing what was occurring, while getting back an amount of compassion and delicate comprehension that she had possessed no ability to conceive. When Mary exited the study, her countenance and eyes were transformed to such a degree that Ida scarcely recognized her.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0005 }

“When he finally wakes up, your father is all right,” she stated, giving a sniff that almost became a sob. “It is a shame he is not awake more frequently. He told me Mrs. Grimble’s death was not my fault, but he said I ought to attempt to recall her positive traits instead of her negative ones. I do not know what positive traits she possessed, except perhaps maintaining a tidy home and producing superior butter. I am certain I nearly scrubbed my arms to exhaustion on her aged kitchen floor with its knots. However, whatever your father tells me from now on is the law for me.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0006 }

In the days that came after, Mary turned out to be quite an uninteresting associate, nevertheless. She admitted to Ida that her hatred of returning to the asylum grew the more she contemplated it. Ida strained her little mind to find any method to prevent this from happening, yet it was Bess Carrow who provided assistance by making a rather shocking proposal.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0007 }

“Mrs. Kerr could perhaps take Mary on her own. Her home is extremely large, and Mr. Kerr constantly desires that she employ assistance. That would be an absolutely wonderful location for Mary. However, it would require her to conduct herself properly.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0008 }

“Oh, Bess, is it possible that Mrs. Kerr might accept her?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0009 }

“Asking her would not cause any trouble,” Bess remarked. Initially, Ida felt incapable of doing so. Her shyness was so intense that requesting a favor from anyone caused her extreme distress. Furthermore, the active, vigorous Mrs. Kerr intimidated her greatly. Although she held her in high regard and thoroughly appreciated visiting her home, going there to request that she take in Mary Stubbs appeared so exceedingly bold that it frightened Ida’s fearful nature.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0010 }

As soon as the Hopetown authorities sent a letter to Mr. Ashdown requesting that Mary be dispatched to them immediately, Mary wept until she fell asleep in the manse attic that evening, which inspired Ida to discover a desperate bravery. On the following evening, she quietly departed from the manse and headed toward the harbour road. Deep within Fern Hollow, she caught the sound of cheerful laughter, yet her path did not lead in that direction. She looked exceedingly pale and was intensely resolute—so focused, in fact, that she paid no attention to the individuals she passed—and old Mrs. Stanley Flagg became rather offended, remarking that Ida Ashdown would turn out to be just as preoccupied as her father once she reached adulthood.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0011 }

Situated mid-way between the Glen and Seven Gulls Point, Miss Winifred's home possessed a tone of pleasing greenish gray, into which its initial bright green color had softened. Ambrose Kerr had surrounded the dwelling with planted trees, a spruce hedge, and an established rose garden. Compared to its state in past years, the residence had become entirely transformed. Visiting the location was a favorite activity for both the manse children and the Hollowmere children. Traversing the ancient harbour road offered a lovely stroll, which invariably concluded with an abundantly stocked cooky jar.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0012 }

Way down upon the beach, the foggy ocean was gently washing against the shore. A trio of large vessels was gliding through the port like huge white seabirds. Up the waterway, a schooner was making its approach. Splendid hues, delicate sounds, and an odd enchantment enveloped the realm of Seven Gulls, a place where all people ought to have been joyful. Nevertheless, as Ida went through the entrance to Miss Winifred’s property, her limbs had nearly given out on her.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0013 }

On the veranda, Miss Winifred was by herself. Mr. Kerr’s presence had been hoped for by Ida. Encouragement would have been found in his being there, because he was so twinkly, hearty, and big. Sitting upon the little stool that Miss Winifred carried outside, she attempted to consume the doughnut that Miss Winifred handed to her. Although it lodged in her throat, she swallowed frantically so Miss Winifred would not take offense. Speech was impossible for her; pallor remained on her face; and Miss Winifred decided that the child was experiencing some distress because her large, dark-blue eyes appeared so piteous.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0014 }

“What are you thinking about, dearie?” she inquired. “It is obvious that something is troubling you.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0015 }

A desperate gulp was how Ida downed the final piece of doughnut.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0016 }

“Mrs. Kerr, will you not accept Mary Stubbs?” she asked in a pleading manner.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0017 }

Miss Winifred gave a blank look.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0018 }

“Keep Mary Stubbs? Is taking her what you mean by that, for me?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0019 }

“Yes—keep her—adopt her,” Ida said eagerly, taking heart once the ice had been broken. “Oh, Mrs. Kerr, please do. Returning to the asylum is not what she wants—she cries every night over it. Being sent to another hard place frightens her so much. And she is so smart—nothing exists that she cannot do. I know taking her is something you would not regret.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0020 }

“Such a thing had never crossed my mind,” Miss Winifred stated, feeling somewhat helpless.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0021 }

“Will you not consider it?” begged Ida.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0022 }

“However, my dear, help is not something I desire. The labor in this place is completely within my own capacity to manage. Furthermore, had I actually required assistance, having a home girl is something I never imagined appealing to me.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0023 }

The brightness faded from the eyes of Ida. Her lips quivered. Rejoining her stool, she sat down, transformed into a pitiable small emblem of letdown, and started weeping.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0024 }

“Don’t—dearie—don’t,” Miss Winifred cried out in upset, as she was completely unable to endure causing pain to a youngster. “I am not refusing to accept her—yet the notion is so novel that it has simply thrown me into confusion. I need time to reflect upon it.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0025 }

“Mary is remarkably clever,” Ida repeated.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0026 }

“Humph! That’s what I’ve been told. I’ve been told she uses profanity, as well. Is it correct?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0027 }

“I haven’t ever actually heard her use curse words,” Ida admitted, feeling uneasy. “However, I fear she is capable of it.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0028 }

“I trust what you say! Is accuracy in her words a constant thing?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0029 }

“Unless she is fearful of being beaten, I believe she does.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0030 }

“And all the same, you wish for me to accept her!”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0031 }

“Any person must adopt her,” Ida wept. “Any person must care for her, Mrs. Kerr.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0032 }

“It is true. Doing it might be my responsibility, after all,” Miss Winifred remarked, sighing. “Anyway, I must discuss the matter with Mr. Kerr. Therefore, refrain from mentioning it for the time being. Have another doughnut, my dear.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0033 }

Ida accepted the item and consumed it, displaying a improved appetite.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0034 }

“Doughnuts are a great favorite of mine,” she admitted “They are never made by Aunt Martha. Miss Tabitha at Hollowmere bakes them, though, and she occasionally allows us a full plate in Fern Hollow. Are you aware of my course of action when a craving for doughnuts strikes and none are available, Mrs. Kerr?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0035 }

“No, my dear. What is it?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0036 }

“I retrieve my mother’s former cookbook to peruse the recipe for doughnuts, as well as the additional recipes. Their descriptions are delightful. This is my habitual reaction whenever hunger strikes me, particularly following a dinner of the same old thing. Subsequent to that, I peruse the recipes for fried chicken alongside the ones for roast goose. My mother possessed the ability to prepare every one of those delicious dishes.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0037 }

“If Mr. Ashdown fails to find a wife, those manse children are going to starve to death eventually,” Miss Winifred said to her spouse in a state of indignation once Ida had left. “Yet he will not—so how do we handle this? Furthermore, Ambrose, do we accept this Mary-creature?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0038 }

“Yes, take her,” Ambrose said briefly.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0039 }

“That is typical of a man,” his wife stated in despair. “‘Take her’—as though nothing else mattered. Trust me, there are one hundred matters to take into account.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0040 }

“Take her—and we will think about them later, Winifred,” her spouse uttered.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0041 }

Ultimately, Miss Winifred brought her along and went upstairs to inform the Hollowmere inhabitants of her choice prior to anything else.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0042 }

“How wonderful!” Nell exclaimed with joy. “Miss Winifred, I was wishing you’d decide to do just that. My desire is for that unfortunate youngster to find a fine home. At one time, I too was an orphan girl without a home, exactly as she is.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0043 }

“I fail to believe that this Mary-creature is or ever will resemble you to any great extent,” Miss Winifred gloomily answered back. “She is a feline of a different shade. However, she remains a human being possessing an immortal soul that requires saving. Having put my hand to the plough, trust me, I possess a shorter catechism along with a fine-toothed comb and intend to perform my obligation toward her.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0044 }

The information was taken in by Mary with a subdued sense of gratification.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0045 }

“This is a greater piece of fortune than I had anticipated,” she remarked.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0046 }

“You’ll need to watch your step around Mrs. Kerr,” Bess stated.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0047 }

“Indeed, that lies within my power,” snapped Mary. “My understanding of proper conduct when I desire it matches yours precisely, Bess Carrow.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0048 }

“It is not right for you to speak vulgarly, Mary, as you are aware,” Ida remarked with concern.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0049 }

“I reckon the thought would scare her to death,” Mary chuckled, her pale eyes glimmering with mischievous delight at the notion. “You can rest easy, Ida, though. From now on, I will be the picture of innocence. I shall be on my absolute best behavior.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0050 }

“Or utter falsehoods,” Grace chimed in.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0051 }

“Not even to escape being whipped?” Mary begged.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0052 }

“Izzy declared, “At no time will Mrs. Kerr give you a whipping—at no time.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0053 }

“Won’t she?” Mary asked in a doubtful tone. “Should I ever end up in a spot where I am not beaten, I will certainly consider it heaven. There will be no danger of my lying at that point. I am not partial to telling them—I would prefer not to, if given the choice.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0054 }

A picnic was held in Fern Hollow to celebrate Mary prior to her leaving the manse the following day, and when night came, each child of the manse presented her with a memento chosen from their small collection of cherished possessions. Rupert presented his Noah’s ark to her, whereas Tobias handed over his second best jew’s-harp. Grace provided a small hairbrush that featured a mirror embedded in its rear, an item Mary had forever viewed as truly marvelous. Ida wavered in deciding between a worn beaded purse and a vibrant illustration showing Daniel in the lion’s den, ultimately letting Mary select whichever she preferred. Mary truly longed for the beaded purse, yet understanding how much Ida cherished it, she said,
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0055 }

“Hand over Daniel. I’d rather take that one since I have a fondness for lions. Although I do wish Daniel had been devoured by them. The story would have been far more thrilling.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0056 }

When it was time for bed, Mary persuaded Ida to share her sleep.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0057 }

“This is the final time,” she remarked, “and rain is falling this evening, and I detest resting up in that room by myself in the rain because of the cemetery. On pleasant evenings I do not care, but during a night such as this the only thing visible to me is the rain falling over those aged white tombstones, while the wind about the windowpane sounds like those deceased individuals attempting to enter and weeping because they fail.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0058 }

“Rainy nights are to my liking,” stated Ida, as they lay snuggled beside one another inside the small attic room, “and the Carrow girls enjoy them too.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0059 }

“When I am nowhere near cemeteries, I do not care about them,” Mary remarked. “Were I by myself in this place, my loneliness would cause me to weep uncontrollably. The thought of departing from everyone makes me feel terribly miserable.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0060 }

“I feel certain Mrs. Kerr will permit you to visit and play in Fern Hollow very frequently,” Ida stated. “And Mary, you are going to be a well-behaved girl, aren’t you?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0061 }

“Oh, I’ll try,” Mary sighed. “But being good—on the inside, I mean, and not just the outside—will not be as simple for me as it is for you. My relations were much greater scalawags than yours.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0062 }

“Your people were bound to possess a few positive traits alongside their negative ones, however,” Ida reasoned. “It is those you ought to fulfill, ignoring their shortcomings.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0063 }

“I do not think they possessed a single redeeming virtue,” Mary remarked morosely. “I was never told about any. My grandfather possessed wealth, yet people claim he was a scoundrel. No, I must simply make my own way and try to succeed as well as possible.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0064 }

“And God will assist you, as you are aware, Mary, should you request it of Him.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0065 }

“I am not certain of that.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0066 }

“Oh, Mary. You are aware that we prayed to God to provide a home for you, and He granted it.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0067 }

“I fail to comprehend how He was involved,” Mary answered back. “You were the one who suggested it to Mrs. Kerr.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0068 }

“Yet it was placed within her heart by God to adopt you. Had He not done so, no amount of my urging her would have achieved anything.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0069 }

“Well, you could be right about that,” conceded Mary. “Listen to me, I don't hold a grudge against God, Ida. I am prepared to grant Him an opportunity. However, truly, I feel He resembles your father immensely—simply distracted and ignoring a person nearly all the time, yet occasionally snapping to attention out of nowhere and proving exceptionally nice and caring and wise.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0070 }

“Oh, Mary, no!” Ida cried out in horror. “God is not at all like father—I mean He is a thousand times kinder and better.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0071 }

“Provided He is as fine as your father He will suit me,” Mary said. “While your father was speaking with me I had the feeling that I could not ever be wicked again.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0072 }

“It would be better if you spoke with father regarding Him,” Ida sighed. “His ability to explain everything far surpasses mine.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0073 }

Mary gave her word, “Well, I shall do that very thing, the moment he awakens again. When he conversed with me in the study during that evening, he made me understand completely that Mrs. Grimble was not killed by my prayers. My thoughts have been untroubled from then on, though I remain extremely careful regarding prayer. It strikes me that relying on the old verse is the most secure approach. Look here, Ida, it appears to my way of thinking that were a person required to pray to someone, choosing the devil would be preferable to choosing God. Since God possesses goodness, as you claim at any rate, He is not going to cause you damage, whereas based on everything I am able to gather, the devil requires soothing. It strikes me as logical to speak to him, ‘Kind devil, I ask that you do not entice me. I request that you simply let me be.’ Wouldn't you agree?”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0074 }

“Oh, no, no, Mary. I feel certain that praying to the devil couldn’t be proper. Furthermore, it would be useless since he is evil. Doing so might rile him up, making him even worse.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0075 }

“Well, regarding this issue of God,” Mary stated obstinately, “because the two of us are unable to resolve it, discussing it further is pointless until an opportunity arises for us to learn the truth about it. Until that time, I will manage as well as I am able by myself.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0076 }

“Our mother would be able to inform us about all of it if she were still living,” Ida remarked, sighing.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0077 }

“I wish she hadn’t died,” Mary remarked. “I am at a loss as to what will happen to you children after my passing. Regardless, make an effort to maintain some neatness in the home. It is disgraceful how folk gossip regarding its condition. Furthermore, before you realize it, another wife will be taken by your father, placing you all in a less favored position.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0078 }

Ida felt a sudden shock. Never had the thought occurred to her that her father might remarry. Disliking the notion, she remained still, overwhelmed by the cold feeling it brought.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0079 }

“Stepmothers are terrible beings,” Mary continued. “If I were to inform you about everything I know concerning them, I could freeze your blood. A stepmother belonged to the Wilson children, who lived across the road from Grimble’s. To them, she behaved just as horribly as Mrs. Grimble behaved to me. If a stepmother comes into your life, it will be dreadful.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0080 }

“I feel certain we shall not,” Ida remarked with a quiver in her voice. “Papa will never take another wife.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0081 }

“I anticipate he will be driven into it,” Mary remarked somberly. “Every single maiden in the colony is pursuing him. They are impossible to outwit. Furthermore, the trouble with stepmothers is their habit of turning your father against you. Your importance to him would completely disappear. His support would invariably go to her and her offspring. You see, she would convince him of your total wickedness.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0082 }

“Mary, I wish you hadn’t shared this with me,” Ida exclaimed. “It fills me with such unhappiness.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0083 }

“My intention was merely to give you a warning,” Mary remarked, sounding somewhat contrite. “To be sure, your father is so preoccupied that he may not even consider taking another wife. Still, being ready for it is preferable.”
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0084 }

A considerable time after Mary was sleeping peacefully, little Ida remained awake, tears causing her eyes to sting. Oh, how terrible it would prove if her father were to marry a person who caused him to hate her along with Tobias, Grace, and Rupert! It was impossible for her to endure it—simply impossible!
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0085 }

Mary had refrained from putting any such venom as Miss Winifred had dreaded into the manse children’s thoughts. Nevertheless, with the finest motives, she had definitely managed to cause a bit of trouble. She slept without dreams, however, as Ida remained awake and rain came down while the wind moaned about the aged gray manse. Meanwhile, the Rev. John Ashdown completely neglected to retire for the night owing to his absorption in reading a biography of St. Augustine. Dawn was gray by the time he completed it and proceeded upstairs, grappling with the issues of two millenniums past. Finding the door to the girls’ chamber open, he observed Grace fast asleep, flushed and lovely. He pondered where Ida could be. It crossed his mind that she might have gone across to “stay all night” alongside the Carrow girls. She engaged in this now and then, considering it a splendid pleasure. John Ashdown uttered a sigh. It seemed to him that where Ida was should not be an unknown matter to him. Cecelia would have exercised superior care over her than that.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0086 }

If Cecelia remained by his side even now! What beauty and cheerfulness she used to possess! The ancient manse located at Juneford had resounded so greatly with her singing! Then she departed with such suddenness, carrying off her mirth and melodies while leaving hush behind—departing so abruptly that his sense of astonishment had never fully faded. How was it possible for her, who was so gorgeous and lively, to pass away?
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0087 }

John Ashdown had never given genuine thought to marrying again. His affection for his wife had been so profound that he felt it impossible to ever love another woman. He entertained a faint notion that Grace would soon reach an age where she could step into her mother’s role. In the meantime, he had to manage as well as possible by himself. Sighing, he proceeded to his bedroom, in which the bed remained unmade. Aunt Martha had overlooked it, whereas Mary had abstained from making it out of fear, as Aunt Martha had instructed her not to interfere with anything in the minister’s chamber. Nevertheless, Mr. Ashdown failed to observe its unmade state. St. Augustine occupied his final thoughts.
{: #nw-v05-c09-p0088 }
